course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Cold War and Decolonization
unit.description: Study how the Cold War divided the world, how colonies won independence, how new states and movements challenged established power, and why the Cold War ended.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a cause of migration from former colonies to Britain and France after 1945?

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.6 key concept: the redrawing of boundaries after independence caused mass migration and conflict
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing migration after the partition of India and the founding of Israel, 1947–1960
stimulusBlocks.text:
The partition of India in 1947 set off one of the largest migrations in history. About 15 million people crossed the new borders, Hindus and Sikhs moving to India and Muslims to Pakistan. Communal violence killed hundreds of thousands, and some estimates reach two million.

When Israel declared independence in 1948, war followed with neighboring Arab states, and about 700,000 Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled from their homes. Migration also flowed toward the former colonial powers: people from the Caribbean and South Asia moved to Britain, and Algerians moved to France, often to fill postwar labor shortages.

questions.prompt: The passage suggests that migration from former colonies to Britain was encouraged by
choices: the Cold War arms race
the partition of Palestine
the end of the Algerian War
postwar labor shortages
questions.explanation: Workers were needed to fill jobs in Britain.
choiceExplanations: The passage does not mention the arms race.
Palestinians fled to neighboring states.
Algerians moved to France.
Workers were needed to fill jobs in Britain.
questions.distinguisher: Algerian migration went to France, not Britain.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, the Suez Crisis ended when
choices: Egypt agreed to return the canal to Britain and France
the superpowers pressured the invaders to withdraw
Nasser was overthrown by the invading armies

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.6 key concept: some newly independent states pursued state-led economic development
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing state-led development in Egypt and India, 1951–1970
stimulusBlocks.text:
Gamal Abdel Nasser came to power in Egypt after army officers overthrew the king in 1952. He broke up large estates and, in 1956, nationalized the Suez Canal, which had been run by a British and French company. Britain, France, and Israel invaded, but pressure from the United States and the Soviet Union forced them to withdraw.

India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, launched Five-Year Plans in 1951 that directed investment into steel, dams, and heavy industry while leaving farms and many businesses in private hands.

questions.prompt: Nasser's nationalization of the Suez Canal is best understood in the context of
choices: the scramble for Africa among European powers
new states' efforts to control their resources
Egypt's alliance with Britain against the Soviets
the founding of the League of Nations after 1919
questions.explanation: New states sought economic independence from former colonial powers.
choiceExplanations: The scramble was in the 1880s.
New states sought economic independence from former colonial powers.
The nationalization challenged Britain.
The League of Nations dated from the 1919 peace settlement, long before 1956.
questions.distinguisher: Britain occupied Egypt in 1882; by 1956 Egypt was reclaiming control.

questions.prompt: Nehru's economic policy described in the passage differed from Soviet planning in that it
choices: left farms and many businesses private
invested heavily in steel and heavy industry
